svg.text: A spine running from the problem (how do neurons combine signals?) through a method built to answer it (PID), into
a fan of empirical findings about where synergy lives, and out to the method's limits and what comes next.

g.text: From the problem to the payoff
Down the page is the article's own order: motivation, tools, the gap those tools leave, the PID framework built to fill
it, a fan of empirical discoveries about synergy, then the method's limits, its future, and a closing summary.

g.title: Brains process information — but how? — New recording tech and new analysis tools now make this question tractable. — → spya-yb735k

Mutual information vs. transfer entropy — shared pattern vs. directed flow — Mutual information shows undirected similarity between neurons; transfer entropy shows directed information flow from one to another. — → spya-mx45r0
But flow alone can't show how inputs combine — Transfer entropy tracks propagation, not how a neuron integrates multiple sources into a new signal. — → spya-dhy39x
g.text: But flow alone can't show how inputs combine

g.title: PID: split joint information into redundant, unique, synergistic parts — Partial information decomposition formally separates overlapping, individual, and combination-only information. — → spya-u0wm5e
Needs a choice of redundancy measure — none is universal — The decomposition is underdetermined until one defines redundancy; a dozen competing definitions exist. — → spya-d2quz5
g.text: Needs a choice of redundancy measure — none

g.title: Applying PID to real recordings — Hundreds of cultured cortical neurons, decomposed triad by triad, reveal where synergy concentrates. — → spya-cc282b
Rich-club neurons hold most of the network's synergy — A minority of best-connected neurons account for about 88% of all synergy. — → spya-e3ghxj
Recurrent connections raise synergy; feedback doesn't — Loops between source neurons add to synergy; feedback to the sources mostly doesn't. — → spya-p8by2y
Synergy peaks, then falls, as inputs grow more alike — Mildly correlated sources produce the most synergy; highly correlated ones become redundant instead. — → spya-zfs2z7
In monkeys, redundancy rises during movement — Behaving-animal recordings show the balance of synergy and redundancy shifts with the task at hand. — → spya-aqcngt
Practical limits: data type, sample size, software tools — Choosing a redundancy function and gathering enough data are both real constraints in practice. — → spya-kmgwhs
g.text: Practical limits: data type, sample size,

g.title: Future: moment-by-moment and multi-target PID — Local PID resolves synergy over time; integrated information decomposition extends it to multiple targets. — → spya-zz5xxs
Synergy: neurons compute on patterns, not just totals — The closing summary ties the empirical findings back to what synergy means for neural computation. — → spya-rc5z33

g.text: A chain of logical steps: the discovery that information doesn't simply add up, the algebra that first split it into
parts for two sources, and the lattice machinery needed once there are more than two — all resting on one
still-unsettled choice, the definition of redundancy.

g.title: Joint information isn't just the sum of each source's part — Summing each parent neuron's individual information about the target doesn't equal the information from all of them together. — → spya-h5dz45
g.text: Joint information isn't just the sum of each

g.title: Whole > parts means synergy; whole < parts means redundancy — Extra information beyond the sum signals genuine integration (synergy); a shortfall signals double-counted overlap (redundancy). — → spya-e94ury
g.text: Whole > parts means synergy; whole < parts

g.title: Williams & Beer found how to split it algebraically — Their partial information decomposition framework made this split exact, not just descriptive. — → spya-t02v4p
g.text: Williams & Beer found how to split it

g.title: Two parents: redundant + unique(1) + unique(2) + synergistic — With two source neurons, the joint information splits into four distinct, non-overlapping pieces. — → spya-q2b0e5
Underdetermined — pick one piece to define — Three known mutual-information values but four unknown pieces: defining any one term yields the rest. — → spya-bgsd4n
g.text: Underdetermined — pick one piece to define

g.title: More than two parents: need the partial information lattice — With three or more sources the simple algebra isn't enough; a structured lattice of all possible source combinations is required. — → spya-k378fv
g.text: More than two parents: need the partial

g.title: Lattice atoms computed by Möbius inversion — A recursive formula extracts each unique information atom once a redundancy measure is chosen. — → spya-m37w5y
g.text: Lattice atoms computed by Möbius inversion
Inside: what PID found in real circuits
A chain into a fan and back: recordings feed one overall finding (synergy tracks feedforward flow), which splits into
three parallel discoveries about where and why synergy concentrates, which converge on caveats and then on a result

g.title: 512-channel recordings from cultured mouse cortex — Hundreds of neurons recorded at once, with thousands of source-source-target triads analyzed by PID. — → spya-sw5ukx
Synergy tracks the strength of feedforward information flow — Across 25 recordings, synergy was reliably about a quarter of the feedforward transfer entropy. — → spya-kqkb58
g.text: Synergy tracks the strength of feedforward

g.title: Rich-club triads: 2.7x more synergy, ~88% of total — Densely interconnected 'rich club' neurons are small in number but dominant in synergy. — → spya-fud8q3
Recurrent links help synergy; feedback links don't — Connections between source neurons raised synergy; connections back from target to sources mostly didn't. — → spya-sd9fzd
Synergy peaks then falls as sources grow more alike — Mild similarity between source neurons boosts synergy; too much similarity turns it into redundancy instead. — → spya-ybmve2
g.text: Synergy peaks then falls as sources

g.title: Caveats: bias from simple pairwise flow estimates; culture, not living brain — Results depend on bivariate transfer-entropy networks and on in-vitro cortical cultures, not behaving animals. — → spya-j4cy9j
g.text: Caveats: bias from simple pairwise flow estimates;

g.title: In behaving monkeys, redundancy rises during movement execution — Task demands shift the balance: redundancy increases when reliable transmission to distant muscles matters most. — → spya-t8fayf
g.text: In behaving monkeys, redundancy rises during
